rationale: The old unsafe block existed only to wrap the library's resolve result in the `ArchivedArc` constructor; the new resolve API writes the archived value directly into the caller's `&mut MaybeUninit` out-parameter via the `project_struct!` helper, so the whole construction is delegated to safe library code.

As for `ArchivedArc`, the unsafe `ArchivedRc(...)` construction is replaced by the safe resolver writing into the `&mut MaybeUninit` out-parameter through `project_struct!`, which is a helper whose body is not shown.

`str::from_utf8_unchecked` (UB on invalid UTF-8) is replaced by `to_string_lossy()`, a validity-checked bytes-to-string conversion; the manual `sqlite3_free` also goes away because the `expanded_sql()` result is now owned (secondary: safe wrapper).

The hand-rolled `sqlite3_malloc` + `ptr::copy_nonoverlapping` + null-terminator `alloc` is replaced by delegating to `SqliteMallocString::from_str(...).into_raw()`, a safe helper whose body is not shown.

The `mem::transmute(protocols)` (raw transmute with ambiguous ownership) is replaced by `Box::into_raw(protocols)`, which transfers ownership of the boxed value deliberately to the FFI; the transmute-replaced-by-ownership change is the whole fix.

The platform-specific `libc::send` on a raw fd/raw socket (and the raw-fd recv path) is replaced by calling the inner socket's safe `send`/`recv` methods, so the backend type performs the whole operation.

`mem::transmute(&ctx)` laundered a shared reference into a mutable raw pointer; the new code just passes `&mut ctx`, a plain mutable borrow that coerces to the FFI pointer (secondary: `cvt_p`/`try!` turns the null/error check into a checked wrapper).

`unsafe { xcb::cast_event(&event) }` (raw reinterpretation of event bytes) is replaced by matching the typed `xcb::Event::X(x::Event::KeyPress(..))` enum returned by the crate's safe request/reply API, i.e. enum instead of transmute.

The C-style tagged API (`xcb::ClientMessageEvent::new(32, ..)` and tuple value lists) is rewritten onto xcb 1.0 typed enums/structs (`x::ClientMessageData::Data32`, `x::CreateWindow`, `x::Cw::..`), so the event/request representation is now an enum instead of unchecked tagged data (same migration as the sibling xcb examples).

rationale: `unsafe { xcb::cast_event(&event) }` (raw reinterpretation of event bytes) is replaced by matching the typed `xcb::Event::X(x::Event::KeyPress(..))` enum returned by the crate's safe request/reply API, i.e. enum instead of transmute.

`unsafe { xcb::cast_event(&event) }` plus the unchecked union accessor `.u().cc()` are replaced by typed enum matches (`xcb::Event::RandR(randr::Event::Notify(ev))`, `randr::NotifyData::Cc(cc)`), so the payload representation is a safe enum instead of a raw cast.
Dereferencing the `UnsafeCell` pointer obtained from `value.durability.get()` is replaced by `Atomic::load()`, so unsynchronised mutation is expressed through the safe atomic interior-mutability API.
`std::mem::uninitialized()` for the one-byte buffer is replaced by a zero-initialized `[0u8; 1]` array.
`std::mem::uninitialized()` for the three-byte buffer is replaced by a zero-initialized `[0u8; 3]` array.
The `recvbuf` field is zero-initialized with `[0u8; RECVBUF_SIZE]` instead of `std::mem::uninitialized()`.
The `sendbuf` field is zero-initialized with `[0u8; SENDBUF_SIZE]` instead of `std::mem::uninitialized()`.
`set_len` that declared uninitialized capacity as filled is replaced by `resize(end, 0)`, a safe Vec length operation that also initializes the grown region.
`from_raw_parts`/`ptr::read` type-punning of a byte buffer is replaced by `chunks_exact(n)` iterators plus `from_ne_bytes` per chunk, so no raw pointer or reinterpretation remains.
evidence_old: unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(s as *const [u8] as *const u32, s.len() / 4) }

rationale: The unsafe `bytes_mut()` (which handed out `&mut [u8]` over uninitialized capacity) is replaced by the safe `MaybeUninit`-typed variant, and each slot is written with `MaybeUninit::new(...)`, so memory is explicitly initialized before any later `assume_init`.

`AsciiChar::from_unchecked` (a validity-unchecked constructor that can create invalid enum discriminants) is replaced by the validity-checked `AsciiChar::new` inside a branchless array-index expression.
evidence_new: [*self, AsciiChar::new((*self as u8 & 0b101_1111) as char)][self.is_lowercase() as usize]

rationale: `Vec::with_capacity` + `set_len` over uninitialized memory is replaced by `vec![0; n]`, so the buffer is initialized before use.
The `set_len` Vec over uninitialized memory is replaced by a zero-initialized `[0; MAX_SKIP_BUFFER]` array (the read path also moves from `read_exact` to `read` with EOF handling).

The old `std::mem::uninitialized()` array plus `ptr::write` per element is replaced by mapping the range and collecting, then a length-checked `try_into` into the fixed-size array, which is what removes the unchecked uninitialized write (secondary: iterator-based construction).
`MaybeUninit::uninit().assume_init()` (instant UB) is replaced by `MaybeUninit::zeroed()`, which produces properly initialized storage.
The `cancel()` call in the unsafe block is already a safe method; the block is simply dropped.
The `raw_cancel()` call in the unsafe block is already a safe method; the block is simply dropped.
The unsafe block around `g.cancel()` is removed because the method is safe; only a type annotation on `next()` changes.
The hand-written `vec_resize` (raw pointer `ptr::write` plus `set_len` bookkeeping) is replaced by `Vec::resize`, the safe length operation.
`from_raw_parts_mut` over spare capacity, `set_len` and the consume/rewind bookkeeping are replaced by `resize` + a normal slice borrow + `truncate`.
`reserve(256)` + `set_len(capacity())` is replaced by `resize(capacity() + 256, 0)`, a safe capacity/length operation that zero-initializes the extension instead of exposing uninitialized bytes.

`std::slice::from_raw_parts` reinterpretation of the C buffer as `CK_MECHANISM_TYPE` is replaced by `chunks_exact(size_of::<..>())` plus `from_ne_bytes` per chunk, with a length-multiple guard, so the reinterpretation is gone.
The thread-local `UnsafeCell<Waker>` dereferenced as `unsafe { &*l.get() }` is replaced by a `Lazy<Waker>` static that hands out a safe `&Waker`, so the lazy-initialised wrapper does the whole job.

`mem::uninitialized()` for the inline storage is replaced by `MaybeUninit::uninit()`, so the storage is tracked as possibly-uninitialized and only assumed initialized after the element is written (secondary: the inline field type becomes `MaybeUninit`).
The `reset_without_timer` call is safe in the new API, so the SAFETY-comment unsafe block is simply dropped.

The stored `*const T` plus `unsafe { &*self.value }` (and the unsafe Send/Sync impls) are replaced by a stored projection closure and `PhantomData<fn(&T) -> &R>`; `deref` just calls the projection, so the raw-pointer representation disappears.
